notes: Body-free Coverage Registry of strategically relevant publishers and resources, whether or not they are currently onboarded Sources. This is not a complete census of the public web. entries.display_name: Canadian Food Inspection Agency -- Plant Breeders' Rights Register
entries.notes: Source Coverage Gap Closure V1. Structurally similar to the existing CPVO registry integration (app.services.cpvo_registry) -- a real, plain-HTML government PBR register organized by crop kind and botanical name, with a periodic Plant Varieties Journal. No existing adapter or module covers it. Deliberately deferred rather than built here: a correct structured-registry module (mirroring cpvo_registry.py's search/normalize/build_review_draft/persist_drafts/run_*_monitor shape) is real, separately-scoped work, not a quick Source config addition -- forcing it through generic article-feed semantics would misrepresent structured registry data as news.

Source Coverage Gap Closure V1. robots.txt confirmed open with a sitemap index (sitemap_index.xml) -- technically reachable via sitemap_xml, but this is catalog/reference material (variety-by-variety pages), not a recurring news/updates flow the way Fall Creek's own newsroom Source (source-20260824-fall-creek-newsroom) already covers. Deferred: onboarding a second Fall Creek Source for largely-static catalog content did not meet the 'repeatedly yields qualifying material' bar this mission set for grower/marketer sites -- a bounded, one-time catalog capture (not a recurring Source) would be the more honest mechanism if pursued.

Source Coverage Gap Closure V1. robots.txt confirmed open with a sitemap index; no AI-crawler exclusion found. Deferred, not rejected: only 4 existing cited-evidence hits and no confirmed dedicated news/blog leaf sitemap identified during this pass (the sitemap index has not yet been decomposed into its sub-sitemaps) -- worth a follow-up pass once a genuine recurring-content leaf sitemap is confirmed, rather than guessing at one now.

Source Coverage Gap Closure V1. WordPress site; robots.txt open with a sitemap (wp-sitemap.xml), but the standard /feed/ RSS endpoint returned a live HTTP 500 (broken, not blocked). Deferred: narrow single-company investor-relations scope, and the direct-feed path is currently broken -- a sitemap-based fallback is technically possible but adds complexity disproportionate to 3 existing cited-evidence hits for one company's press-release feed alone.
